name: aggregates a branching tree despite reverse delivery order
a single-node root returns one without a shared tree walk
input: one root with no local children

name: concurrent request IDs keep partial sums isolated
input: two count requests in flight over the same three-node tree

name: duplicate child replies cannot inflate the aggregate
input: a root with two leaves receives one leaf reply twice
test:
sent = []
root = AsyncTreeCounter('root', ['left', 'right'], lambda target, message: sent.append((target, dict(message))))
root.receive_message(None, {'type': 'count_request', 'request_id': 'once'})
root.receive_message('left', {'type': 'count_reply', 'request_id': 'once', 'count': 1})
root.receive_message('left', {'type': 'count_reply', 'request_id': 'once', 'count': 1})
root.receive_message('right', {'type': 'count_reply', 'request_id': 'once', 'count': 1})
assert sent[-1] == (None, {'type': 'count_reply', 'request_id': 'once', 'count': 3})
assert root.state == {}
